Which source is the authoritative 'journal'? The transactional ledger of record: one row per posting line, carrying a signed amount and a document reference; debit and credit lines balance per document. Every proposed candidate was put to the balance law, and every one of them failed it.

Which of the proposed candidates is the 'doc_ref'? The document (voucher) reference that groups journal lines into balanced postings. No check can settle this — what the data means is a business fact, not an arithmetic one.

Which of the proposed candidates is the 'account'? The account identifier on the journal, resolvable against a chart of accounts. No check can settle this — what the data means is a business fact, not an arithmetic one.

Which of the proposed candidates is the 'period'? The posting period on the journal, at fiscal-period granularity. No check can settle this — what the data means is a business fact, not an arithmetic one.
Which of the proposed candidates is the 'entity'? The legal entity or company code a posting belongs to. No check can settle this — what the data means is a business fact, not an arithmetic one.

What is missing before the 'subledger_ar' can be tested? The accounts-receivable open items: one row per open receivable with a signed amount, reconcilable against the journal's control account. No proposed candidate could be put to the subledger_equals_gl law at all, so nothing about it has been tested.

Which source is the authoritative 'intercompany'? Paired intercompany postings between two entities that must mirror each other per period. Every proposed candidate was put to the ic_symmetry law, and every one of them failed it.
